lesson_title: Is a Tomato a Fruit? Ask a Botanist
hook_text: To a scientist, a tomato, a bean pod and a mealie grain are all fruits. Here is why.
clip_script: Plants have two big ways to make new plants. Mosses and ferns make spores: specks like dust, with no food inside. They need damp places because their sex cells have to swim. Every other plant makes seeds: a baby plant, a food store and a tough coat, like a lunchbox. Some seed plants keep their seeds naked on cones: pines, our national yellowwood, and cycads that lived with the dinosaurs. Those are gymnosperms, and they have no flowers. The rest wrap their seeds up. They have flowers, and after pollination part of the flower swells into a fruit around the seeds. Those are angiosperms. So in science, a fruit is anything from a flower that holds seeds. Tomato: fruit. Bean pod: fruit. Mealie grain: fruit. Sweet has nothing to do with it.
visual_style: Whiteboard fern dropping dust-like spores; a seed opening like a lunchbox; a pine cone with bare seeds; a flower swelling into a tomato, bean pod and mealie cob, each stamped FRUIT.
pacing: Quick spores-versus-seeds split, a naked-versus-wrapped reveal, a punchy fruit finale.
